topic.readerProblem: A marketer comparing Surfer SEO and AthenaHQ cannot tell whether they are rivals or complements now that Surfer sells AI prompt tracking, what each costs, and which one fits their weekly job.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines name a brand; this guide helps a reader choose between a content-first tool with AI tracking and an AI-visibility-first tool, and when a one-off audit should come before either subscription.

assessment: The page replaces the older premise that Surfer is content-only with what Surfer's own pages now document (AI Tracker, five engines, plans from $82 per month billed yearly) and sets it against AthenaHQ's published Free, Starter and Enterprise plans. It gives a decision rule by weekly job, a price and coverage table, a labeled arithmetic comparison at AthenaHQ's credit unit, an evidence-based note on content scores versus AI citation (Google Search Central, the GEO paper), vendor questions to ask, and a neutral fact box from AEOeye's crawler study. It rests on public vendor pages fetched on 2026-10-03. It deliberately does not claim hands-on testing, does not repeat either vendor's customer results or the 25% citation claim as fact (labeled vendor-reported and unverified), and does not publish unpriced items (AthenaHQ annual price, extra credits, API; Surfer Enterprise).

pricing.billing: Surfer: plans shown per month billed yearly (AI Search Analytics $82, Discovery $49, Standard $99, Pro $182, Peace of Mind $299), Enterprise custom; AthenaHQ: Free, Starter $295 per month, Enterprise custom, add-ons unpriced
pricing.verification: Fetched surferseo.com/pricing and athenahq.ai/pricing with curl on 2026-10-03 and read the raw HTML: Surfer card prices and data-yearly/data-monthly attributes ($82/$95, $49/$59, $99/$119, $182/$219, $299/$359), prompt counts and refresh cadence per plan from the plan-comparison table; AthenaHQ Free $25 credit with 300 credits, Starter $295 per month with 3,600 credits, 1 credit = 1 AI response, add-ons 'contact us'. Recomputed 50 prompts x 5 engines x 30 daily runs = 7,500 and x 4 weekly runs = 1,000 responses.

sources.supports: Surfer plans and prices billed yearly, AI Search Analytics 50 daily prompts across five engines, Discovery with no AI tracking, Standard 25 weekly prompts worded 'across ChatGPT', Pro and Peace of Mind prompt counts, document limits, auto-renewal and yearly billing.
Surfer's AI Tracker: Visibility Score, mention gaps, sentiment, share of voice, five engines, scraping of real interfaces instead of APIs (vendor claim), one prompt tracked across all five models.
Homepage titled 'AI Visibility Platform'; claim that content optimized with Surfer is 25% more likely to be cited by AI (vendor-reported, underlying study not opened).
Content Editor and real-time Content Score, 500+ ranking factors analyzed, Auto-Optimize, internal linking, Surfy writing assistant, Content Audit.
5 August 2026 update: Recommendations now include AI Tracker signals (mentions to pursue, sentiment to fix, topics to cover).

AthenaHQ Free ($25 credit, 300 credits, five platforms), Starter $295 per month with 3,600 credits and 11 models, Enterprise custom, 1 credit = 1 AI response, content recommendations and content optimization agent, GA4/Search Console/Shopify/Webflow integrations, add-on pricing not published.
Definition of generative engine optimization as improving visibility in responses generated by AI systems.
Google says there are no additional requirements or special optimizations for AI Overviews and AI Mode; a page must be indexed and snippet-eligible; SEO fundamentals still apply.

GEO paper (KDD 2024): statistics, quotation and cited-source edits improved visibility 30-40% on Position-Adjusted Word Count; keyword stuffing performed about 10% worse than baseline on Perplexity.ai (read in the full PDF text).
